GrabFood has become my absolute go-to for ordering meals. I am always dependent on them for a good food order and reliable delivery, and they never disappoint. The app offers an amazing selection of restaurants, and the food always arrives fresh and exactly as ordered. What I appreciate the most is the consistency of their riders—deliveries are fast, dependable, and handled with care every single time. It is easily the most trustworthy food delivery service around.

Their payment policy is deeply disappointing and, from a customer’s perspective, feels unnecessarily punitive.

Customers are being prompted to settle an “outstanding payment” without sufficient consideration for whether the issue was caused by a failed transaction, a payment-processing problem, or circumstances beyond the customer’s control. Even more concerning is the expectation that customers must have cards with specific capabilities, such as EMV, e-commerce activation, and 3D Secure, simply to resolve an issue with the service.

A company should make it easier—not harder—for customers to settle legitimate payments. Restricting payment options and placing the burden entirely on the customer creates unnecessary inconvenience and frustration.

Policies like this erode customer trust. I would strongly encourage prospective users to carefully consider the payment policies and customer-service experience before committing to this service. There are plenty of alternatives that offer more reasonable, transparent, and customer-friendly payment processes.

A service should not make customers feel penalized for trying to pay.

The Help Centre is an extremely frustrating example of customer service being replaced by automation without actually addressing the needs of the customer.

Instead of providing meaningful assistance, the AI-driven support system largely directs customers toward generic, pre-written information that does little to resolve specific concerns. When a customer has an unusual problem, a disputed charge, or an issue that does not fit neatly into the options provided, the system becomes effectively useless. You are left navigating automated responses that answer the question it expects you to ask rather than the problem you are actually experiencing.

Automation can certainly improve customer service—but only when there is a clear and accessible way to escalate a concern to a competent human representative. When customers cannot get past an automated help system, it gives the impression that the company is more interested in reducing its support costs than actually helping the people who use its service.

Customer support should be about solving problems, not deflecting them.

If a company cannot provide customers with timely access to a human being when the automated system fails, prospective users should seriously reconsider whether this is a service they want to depend on. A polished interface means very little when there is no meaningful support behind it.

Review Title: Stacked or multiple deliveries causing DELAYS
Review Text:
GrabFood needs to seriously reconsider its practice of assigning multiple deliveries to a single rider.

The issue is not the drivers. The problem is a system that prioritizes order batching over food quality, resulting in longer delivery times, cold meals, melted desserts, and watered-down drinks.

Review Title: Terrible Customer Service and Unfair Practices
Review Text:
I’ve used Grab multiple times in the Philippines, and I have to warn others about the serious issues with this service.

Customer Service is Non-Existent
There’s no way to reach a real agent. If you have a problem with your order, you’re completely stuck. The app offers no meaningful way to communicate with actual support staff—just automated responses that don’t help.

Impossible to Cancel Orders
Once you’ve placed an order, canceling it feels deliberately difficult. The system seems designed to trap you into paying rather than provide a simple cancellation option.

Overcharging and Unfair Pricing
I’ve been overcharged multiple times. There’s no transparency in how fares are calculated, and the prices seem inflated without clear justification.

Monopoly Problem
Grab operates as essentially a monopoly in the Philippines, which means they have no real incentive to improve service or treat customers fairly. With little competition, they can get away with poor practices.

Money Over Customer Care
It’s clear their priority is profit, not customer satisfaction. They don’t respond to complaints. They don’t care about fixing problems. They just want your money.

Review Title: High fares, low to mid standards - Grab needs to do better
Review Text:

Another concern: there should be an option in the app for passengers to decide whether we want to use tollways or not. With already expensive fares, many of us prefer to avoid additional costs. If Grab keeps allowing these issues to persist, they will just keep happening again and again. As a paying customer, I’m tired of it. Grab, please do better.

Review Title: Convenient, but Can Improve in Some Areas.
Review Text:
Grab is a versatile app that has become a go-to for transportation, food delivery, and various on-demand services across Southeast Asia. Whether you need a ride, want food delivered, or are looking to buy groceries, Grab offers an easy and convenient solution right from your smartphone. The app is user-friendly, and the ability to track drivers or delivery progress in real-time is a standout feature that adds to its reliability.

The ride-hailing service is generally quick, and the drivers are usually friendly and professional. Grab’s food delivery service is efficient, and the wide variety of restaurant options ensures that there’s something for everyone. The payment options are also smooth, with the choice of using GrabPay or cash.

However, the app isn’t without its flaws. Surge pricing can sometimes feel excessive, especially during peak hours, and there are occasional delays in food delivery or ride pickups. While the app’s interface is simple, it can occasionally be a bit glitchy, especially after updates. Additionally, customer service is sometimes slow to resolve issues, which can be frustrating if there are problems with orders or rides.

Overall, Grab is an excellent app for those looking for convenience in their daily life, but there’s room for improvement in terms of pricing transparency and app stability.

Review Title: Suggestion for Senior Citizen parents’ sake
Review Text:
Love the app and been using for so long. I also love that previously, I can book for my senior citizen parents using their discount codes. I do this because they don’t know how to use the app and also don’t have internet on their phones. But on Grab’s recent app, codes are no longer used and required every PWD/senior citizen/student to have their own account for the discount. 

Creating their account is easy, also applying for the discount. But the problem here is that for the persons who book for these PWD/senior citizen/student, provided they already have their own accounts, they need to switch accounts just to do that. And before switching, we need to clear cache. So before we get to book for them, we need how many minutes to do so, which is a hassle. Also after that, we need to clear cache and log in to our own accounts again. 

So for the suggestion, either Grab returns the discount codes or have a swift “account switch” in the app for faster process. This will be very very helpful for those PWD/senior citizen/student who can’t use the app or a phone or an internet.

For this, I’ll rate a 4/5 until there’s actually a solution for this.

Review Title: An honest review of a user from a Province wherein Grab does not operate
Review Text:
Grab is an excellent app–for those who's residing/staying in a place where Grab is available, I may say. That would be for those in the big cities like in the Metro. However, the opposite would be for those who's residing in certain provinces wherein Grab is not operating. The app is not friendly for the latter. You have to go through a lot of clicking, pinning, searching, etc. despite saving certain addresses. Just to be able to book a car for, or have a food delivered to someone who's in a place where Grab operates (e.g. Booking from Masbate City a food delivery from a restaurant in Cebu City to be delivered also to someone in Cebu City) is such a hassle. 

This has been my problem with the Grab app for years. It always takes a lot of patience, and somehow tiring, so I opt to use the other App instead. Even if I would very much prefer to order from Grab if not just for the hassle. Not to discredit the good service Grab has done for me during my stays in Manila, Cebu, Legazpi, but it would be better if they improve this, since Grab has a much broader coverage thus having a lot more options in terms of restos, food stalls, coffee shops, etc., to choose from. 

The world changed so much because of the technology available to us right now, so everything and everyone was brought a lot closer despite the distance. I am glad and thankful that Grab has been an instrument for that, even my convenience and safety during my stays in the Metro and in the big cities. So this is just an honest review from someone who's not permanently residing in those big cities, but has loved ones who do, and would very much loved it if Grab would be a lot easier to access for people like me who wishes to show love in their simplest ways to their loved ones from a distance.

The driver finally broke the silence, “Sir diretso pa po ba”.
“Kuya nasan po yung save more?”

He told me stories of power-tripping passengers who gives 1star for breakfast. He experienced, a passenger booked somewhere dark and then lead him to a robbery. He only got to go home only with his underwear. He too was scared that I might’ve been doing the same thing. We were both terrified with this experience. Luckily, I was with a commendable driver.

I gave 5 stars to the driver. And an additional 350 php which was the fare set by the grab app and he showed me. Imagine how far the drop off set by the app from my supposed drop off. Grab(-Car, -Share) in the Philippines largely operates as a monopoly and therefore has a stranglehold on the market with little accountability to its customers. 

Many drivers seem to be ill-trained, lost in the Metro without Waze. Why aren’t they trained or even encouraged to familiarize themselves with the locale? They can also be trained to communicate with passengers on how best to reach the various destinations. 

Some co-passengers on Share are terrible. Are they penalized? Can there be a rating system for passengers from drivers and fellow passengers? And if one is implemented, can there be transparency for the criteria and metrics? Some co-passengers make the GrabShare wait excessively. Other passengers input the wrong drop-off points and insist that the drivers take them to the correct ones. The three-minute pre-cancellation is the grace period (though it could be brought up to five minutes, same as GrabCar) and drivers should be obligated to cancel on truant passengers. 

The app runs slow randomly abd sporadically. If there are system/server issues, there should be transparency and users should be made aware of this. Although admittedly, the interface has improved a lot. 

Why is it no longer possible to call a customer support hotline when users have issues like this? This used to be possible. The Help Center is not very helpful and having to report issues by typing is tedious and there isn’t always a response or updates to supposedly pending cases. 

Et cetera. Et cetera. 

Competition should enter the Philippine market. 

- frustrated (and entrapped) Grab user with first-world problems

Review Title: GRAB = safe ride home + polite & decent drivers + almost brand new vehicles models
Review Text:
Warning: Lengthy review
I know nobody or nothing is perfect but this is my review/opinion so i hope whoever reads this that doesn’t feel the same way, just ignore me ok. Respect my post & i’ll do the same for you ok.
I gave 5 stars to GRAB or more if it permits (in exaggeration lol)
Let me tell u my story;
Too many things are happening at once at that moment; heartbreak, headache, tears, i can’t even find a seat at Starbucks at that time, i can’t even see clearly (tears), holding it in, chest pain; I just decided to go home but it rained heavily, there are few taxi cabs that are lined up outside so i started to approach them, they rolled down their window; “Mam saan po?” as soon as they heard where I’m going, they said, “Mam hindi ko po alam yan eh sa iba ka nalang sumakay” or “Mam dito lang ako sa area na to”. Ni wala man lang nag-offer na taaasan nalang ang rate kc papatulan ko at uwing-uwi na ko & At that moment, I don’t care anymore kung magkano basta makauwi period. All of them had different reasons, none of them gave me a ride home. (Taga-Marikina lang ako, sabi ng isang driver gusto nila yung magpapahatid lang daw sa malalapit para makabalik din sila agad sa pila) Well.. thats ok “minamalas ata ako” i said to myself. My son suggested “Mom use your GRAB app” I haven’t tried GRAB in a long time because i have my own car but unfortunately it was coding that day & I had to meet a client. As soon as i tried, i just typed in the usual then waited to be booked, in less than a minute, someone accepted my request, wow i said to myself, why didn’t i thought of this? Having to ask all the cab drivers to give me a ride home, i felt like I’m begging them. Surely you’d ask, “Bakit nga ba hindi nalang agad nag-grab?”, my answer is this: May common sense tayo diba? Nasa harap ko na yung taxi so anong gagawin ko? Pero waley eh kaya nga nagtry ng Grab. Buti hindi namimili yung mga grab driver, i felt safe kase lumalabas kaagad ung profile ng driver with picture at info ng sasakyan, screenshot lang then send to family or partner at higit sa lahat, amoy brand new ung sasakyan 😊👍
Sana maging ganito lahat ng public ride sa pilipinas. Wala pangarap lang. Yung iba kung tingin nyo OA ako. Balakajan lol 😂

Review Title: Still doesn’t hold a candle to Uber
Review Text:
I am writing this review on this day that marks Uber’s final day of operations in the Philippines. I downloaded the Grab app at the same time I downloaded Uber back in 2014. But because of the better features on the Uber app and the overall better service by Uber cars and drivers, I booked Uber 99% of the time. Uber fares were also cheaper. The past year has seen a rise in the advertisement that Grab has taken from its merchant supporters and irritable pop-ups each time you open the app are not helping. Their Help Centre needs a little push when returning calls for lost or left items as well.
Grab’s finer points would be having a (1) rewards program that allows its riders to use points they’ve accumulated each time they complete a ride, for use with affiliated merchants or to take off P50 or P100 from a current booking (given how high their fares are, I almost always used up my rewards); (2) an efficient delivery service via motorcycle for those days that I need to send small packages within the metro.
Apart from these 2, that’s it. The riding public knows all the negatives that many Grab drivers do. 
It would be nice if Grab ownership REALLY listens to its riders and starts to act on making the overall riding experience pleasant. But, it’s a money-making business after all. And I cannot wait for competition to step up. For now, I’m back to taking public commute.

Some context: 
At the time I rated this app, I came home from a local fiesta while it was raining. All of the taxis were full and I couldn't get a cab. The route where I was waiting started to pile-up and I had to use Grab to get a ride home. The difficult part was me meeting with my driver. Thanks to the gps and messaging feature, I was able to stay in contact with my driver. We both agreed that I'd try to get to him because the roads were closed due to people staying in the middle of the street. I was about 10 feet from my driver when my battery died. I was still able to note down about where he was on the road and thanks also to the feature of describing the vehicle, I was able to find my driver, despite the crazy mess! If it wasn't for Grab or all other ride sharing apps, I would've walked all the way to my destination. The best feature about this app is the versatility it gives you when both you and your driver are having a hard time getting to a place in order to meet. You're connected with your driver and you'll arrive safe. I gave my driver a tip and I rated him excellent. These apps deserve 10 stars instead of 5.
